brief: August US payrolls rose 162,000 (private +127,000) versus 55,000 consensus, with prior revisions adding 55,000 more jobs, lifting the three-month private-employment average to 75,000, above the 0-60,000 breakeven range, while unemployment held at 4.1% as participation rose alongside hiring. Combined with July PCE inflation at 3.7% year-on-year (above expectations) and hawkish Jackson Hole comments from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, this pushed market-implied odds of a September hike from about 50% to roughly 60%, and the S&P 500 fell 0.4% on the news. UBS changed its Fed base case from unchanged rates through 2026 to two 25bp hikes, in September and December, taking the fed funds range from 3.50-3.75% to 4.00-4.25%, citing Warsh's hawkishness, supply-bottleneck inflation risk (weaker ISM/PMI supplier-delivery readings), and firm employment and activity data. A second hike could be postponed if inflation cools sharply through October. UBS also raised its Treasury yield forecasts (2-year to 4.25% by June 2027, 10-year to 4.5%) but stays constructive on global equities, arguing the same AI capex, resilient growth, and earnings strength driving the hawkish shift means higher yields cause only short-term volatility rather than undermining the medium-term case.
